source.objective: explore the area and do not pass from the same cells to cover more

refinement_request: Revise the exploration specification to improve total coverage beyond 63.75 percent while preserving fixed collision avoidance. Use the event statistics and previous design to justify the changes.

explanation.event_selection: We restrict the automaton to the controllable movement events: "task_move_forward", "task_rotate_clockwise", and "task_rotate_counterclockwise". These events directly impact robot motion and coverage. Other available events are either uncontrollable observations or not relevant for high-level exploration and coverage enforcement.
explanation.transition_design: The new specification is structured to reduce repeated forward movements without rotation, to diversify the robot’s movement path and reduce retracing over the same cells. From any initial condition, the robot may move forward or rotate. After a forward move ("recent_forward"), the supervisor is encouraged to follow with a rotation to disrupt long straight runs, thus increasing the likelihood of covering new areas. After a rotation ("recent_rotate"), the supervisor can choose to move forward (start exploring a new direction) or rotate again. This design enables frequent direction changes, which breaks up long straight trajectories (as in the previous design), helping to avoid coverage loss due to repeated cell revisits. All states except the initial transient are marked, allowing repeated alternation of moves and rotations. The structure eliminates possible deadlock and strongly encourages behavioral diversity for maximal area coverage.
explanation.feedback_response: The previous design allowed arbitrary long sequences of 'task_move_forward', resulting in robots frequently re-entering already visited cells, as evidenced by only 61.25% coverage. This revision introduces explicit state memory to favor alternating movement and rotation, thus encouraging path diversity and limiting the likelihood of local cell revisitation. It is expected to improve area coverage by creating more varied exploration patterns among robots without interfering with collision avoidance.
